messages:
alex_w: Noticing a surge of container restarts on node gpu-prod-12 around 09:08 UTC. Crash logs consistently show "CUDA illegal memory access" and "misaligned device address". Opening an incident thread here.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — high-priority GPU runtime crashes in us-west-2. PD notifications sent to oncall rotation.

sophia_k: Grabbed a sample stack from the crashed container (09:09):

```
ServingRuntime: allocator.cu:412: realloc_device_chunk: CUDA error 700: an illegal memory access was encountered
Backtrace:
  at runtime/kv_store.c:128
  at runtime/evict.cu:76
  at runtime/launch_core.cc:58
Signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
```

chris_r: Any recent rollouts? We pushed a small optimization for prefix KV prefetch ~5h ago.

alex_w: Yes that canary reached ~25% earlier this morning. Crash rate increased after that window. Might be a regression under concurrent eviction.

infra-ml: I attempted a local stress run with long-context workloads and concurrent session requests and hit the same illegal access. Looks like a pointer used post-remap during the fallback pagewalk path.

ops-amy: Quick mitigation proposal: cordon+drain gpu-prod-12 to stop new pods landing there, increase capacity on the fallback pool (gpu-fallback-usw2), and flip the runtime flag KV_FAST_PATH=false in the gateway to force the slower but safe path. Which should we do first?

alex_w: Cordon+drain first, then scale fallback and flip config on canaries. Avoid a full rollback unless the config flip fails.

ops-amy: Executing now:
```
kubectl cordon gke-usw2/gpu-prod-12
kubectl drain gke-usw2/gpu-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl scale deploy/serving-runtime -n inference --replicas=18 --selector=pool=gpu-fallback-usw2
```

oncall-bot: TRAFFIC POLICY: preferring pool=gpu-fallback-usw2 for new requests (override 30m).

alex_w: Customer impact check: @cust-success-jake can you scan top customers for 5xxs and timeouts? We saw a small spike to ~0.3% errors in the last 10m.

cust-success-jake: Checking now. Early look shows acme-ai and quickdocs had brief 500 responses between 09:07-09:12. Both notified, no data loss reported.

infra-ml: Repro notes: two concurrent requests for the same session can cause an eviction to start while a pagewalk remaps a device pointer. The memcpy uses the old pointer without a memory-fence after the swap -> illegal device address on GPU.

sophia_k: Two mitigation routes: 1) serialise eviction per session ID (cheap config change), or 2) flip off the fast prefetch/evict path (lower performance but broad safety). I prefer 2 for speed.

alex_w: Agreed. Flip on canaries first. If stable for 10m, rollout to prod in waves.

ops-amy: Pushed runtime gateway config to canaries: `KV_FAST_PATH=false`. Monitoring.

infra-ml: Collecting coredumps and NVML debug logs. Save point commands I used locally:
```
export NVML_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -o cat > /var/log/kubelet-gpu-prod-12.log
sudo cp /var/log/nvidia* /mnt/incident/
```

oncall-bot: COREDUMP SAVED — /mnt/incident/serving-runtime.28471.core.gz

chris_r: Assigning: I'll lead the root-cause and patch work (kernel race hypothesis). Sophia, coordinate the config rollouts and customer comms. Alex you own incident notes.

sophia_k: Canary metrics: illegal/cuda errors dropped from 6/min -> 0.5/min within 2 minutes of the canary flip. No regressions in latency observed. Rolling to next prod wave (4 clusters at a time).

alex_w: Drafting customer notice: "We detected transient inference errors in US-WEST-2 due to an interaction between a runtime eviction optimization and GPU address remapping. We've rerouted traffic away from affected nodes, applied a temporary safe-path config, and are rolling it across the region. We'll post an update in 30 minutes"

cust-success-jake: Sent to impacted customers. Both acknowledged and will wait for further updates.

ops-amy: Prod config flip in progress: setting KV_FAST_PATH=false across us-west-2 gateway ring.

infra-ml: Observability: error-rate reduced from 0.3% -> 0.04% after the first prod wave. No new OOMs on drained node.

chris_r: Working on deterministic repro harness. Plan: add atomic pointer-swap + explicit memory-fence before any device memcpy in evict path. Will validate on CI and canary before hotspot patch.

sophia_k: Also adding a temporary alert rule: `cuda_illegal_count > 5/min` triggers a suggestion to cordon nodes with tag region:us-west-2.

oncall-bot: TEMP ALERT ADDED: cuda_illegal_count > 5/min => post auto-cordon suggestion in thread.

alex_w: Handoff: I'm offshift in 25m. If metrics remain stable for 30m, mark mitigated and close. If not, escalate to kernel-team and prepare rollback of the prefetched-kv change.

chris_r: Acknowledged. I'll watch the window and coordinate the kernel escalation if needed.

sophia_k: Runbook entry saved: "/runbooks/incident-cuda-illegal" includes steps: cordon/drain, flip KV_FAST_PATH, collect coredumps, and rollback instructions.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, traffic rerouted, customers notified. Next automated update +30m.

alex_w: Thanks all. Passing lead to chris for the RCA and patch tracking.

pagerduty-bot: HANDOFF RECORDED: new oncall chris_r. Previous oncall acknowledged.
